response.sql: SELECT AVG(TG) AS avg_tg, AVG(WBC) AS avg_wbc FROM Laboratory WHERE WBC >= 6.5 AND TG IS NOT NULL;

assumptions.assumption: A high WBC count means WBC is greater than or equal to 6.5. The request says 'cutoff' without saying whether the boundary is inclusive.

'Laboratory records' means rows in the Laboratory table, not distinct patients. Rows with a NULL TG are excluded so both averages cover the same set of records. WBC is never NULL in the filtered set because the WBC comparison already excludes it.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat 6.5 as a strict threshold, so only records with WBC above 6.5 count as high.
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG(TG) AS avg_tg, AVG(WBC) AS avg_wbc FROM Laboratory WHERE WBC > 6.5 AND TG IS NOT NULL;

alternatives.interpretation: Compute each average over all high-WBC records and ignore only the NULLs inside each average, so the WBC average is not limited to rows that also have a TG value.
alternatives.sql: SELECT (SELECT AVG(TG) FROM Laboratory WHERE WBC >= 6.5) AS avg_tg, (SELECT AVG(WBC) FROM Laboratory WHERE WBC >= 6.5) AS avg_wbc;
